subject: Social Science
summary: 117 Tapestry of the Past 6 – The Age of Reorganisation The Age of Reorganisation CHAPTER 6 By continuous living tradition and a vital power of rejuvenescence, this land has readjusted itself through unnumbered transformations. — Jagdish Chandra Bose (1917) 1. Why is the period that followed the Maurya empire sometimes called the ‘Age of Reorganisation’? What were the values or principles that guided emperors of that period? How did foreign invaders assimilate into Indian society and contribute to cultural confluence? A glimpse of the art from the age of reorganisation 118 Exploring Society: India and Beyond | Grade 7 Part 1 Bhavisha and Dhruv had recovered from their journey to the Maurya empire and were itching for another adventure. They decide to use Itihāsa again and landed in a new historical period. They came across a collection of art pieces, each one quite different from the other. (See Fig. 6.1.1) They wondered —could these artefacts belong to multiple kingdoms rather than just one? In this chapter we will travel over a fairly long period.
